literal: Those who do work, one's own relatives, and enemies, thus in that manner, everyone, investigating is espionage.
translation: Espionage consists of watching everyone closely—those who perform state duties, one's own relatives, and one's enemies.
modern: அரசுப் பணிகளைச் செய்பவர்கள், தன் உறவினர்கள், பகைவர்கள் என்று சொல்லப்படும் எல்லாரையும் கண்காணித்து ஆராய்வதே ஒற்றாடல் ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the comprehensive scope of a ruler's intelligence network. The poet lists three vital groups that must be kept under surveillance: 'vinai-ceyvār' (officials executing state duties), 'cuṟṟam' (the ruler's own relatives), and 'vēṇṭātār' (declared enemies). By watching officials, the ruler ensures loyalty and efficiency; by watching relatives, internal conspiracies are prevented; and by watching enemies, external threats are anticipated. True espionage ('oṟṟu') leaves no one unobserved, ensuring the stability of the state through complete awareness.
